verdict.rationale: Skyfire documents that its JWT tokens conform to the open KYAPay protocol, a published industry specification, so developers build against a named, open token format. The evidence does not show a protocol version, a machine-readable schema, or conformance tooling. The introspect API only checks whether a token is usable at runtime, and the OpenAPI probe returned 404 on every candidate path. Charging, wallets and settlement remain Skyfire-proprietary APIs. missing for 10: protocol versioning, published machine-readable schema (OpenAPI/JSON schema), conformance or validation test tooling, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can build against a versioned commerce protocol with a published schema and conformance or validation tooling

citations.quote: All Skyfire-issued tokens conform to the open KYAPay protocol, an industry specification for identity-linked payment credentials purpose-built for autonomous systems.
A KYAPay token is a signed, interoperable credential that packages agent identity and payment intent into a verifiable envelope.
